gaps: Potential water-allocation conflict is a qualitative NAP risk. Named contamination-risk locations must not be turned into dispute hotspots; no full violence mechanism or reverse-FCV chain was verified.
The 2026 susceptibility model uses 2007 land cover and equal weights and lacks independent validation; its classes are not event probabilities or current exposure counts.
Municipal interviews are selective and ministry preparedness accounts are self-reported historical activities, not representative performance audits.
South Oropouche figures are launch-stage targets for a four-year project, not verified current delivery or achieved reach.

executive_assessment.text: Named health-risk locations and South Oropouche/Port of Spain corridor findings provide local differentiation, with qualitative plan and unvalidated susceptibility-model limits.

Municipal staffing, planning and funding constraints coexist with disaster-management units and community warning systems. Historical training and system descriptions do not establish response effectiveness.
South Oropouche launch plans and beneficiary/ecosystem targets are prospective; the registry does not verify current completion or measured resilience effects.
